subject: Next steps: SLO matrix & streaming constraints for OpsCloud integration
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <claire@opscloud.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: SLO matrix & streaming constraints for OpsCloud integration

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance/operational constraints before we kick off a benchmark: 

Key SLOs we discussed (baseline ask):
- Interactive widget target: P99 latency <= 150 ms for short exchanges (<= 512 tokens total, streaming enabled).
- Long-form assistants / batch jobs: P99 latency acceptable up to 1.0 s for end-to-end (8k input+output) but interactive UX prefers streaming token start < 250 ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 1,000 req/min with sustained periods at 2,500 req/min for 10-15 minutes (burst).
- Concurrency: typical steady concurrency ~50; launch-day spikes up to ~200.
- Streaming: must support partial token emission (server push / SSE or websocket) so frontend can render tokens as they arrive.
- Context window: mixture of short prompts (70% < 512 tokens) and extended contexts for retrieval-augmented flows (30% up to 8k).

Operational notes / constraints from your team I captured:
- VPC/private deployment preferred (sensitive metadata).
- Need an expected minimum GPU footprint for procurement planning.
- Security: SOC2 + audit logs required (we'll include evidence).

Attachments: OpsCloud_SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (blank SLO matrix with columns we promised to fill), redwood_perf_profiles_q3.pdf (examples of benchmark numbers across model families).

Proposed next steps:
1) OpsCloud: share 1) representative prompt set (CSV) and 2) a brief traffic shape (RPS/concurrency by hour) — target by EOD Tue (6/22).
2) Redwood (Ben): propose a canary benchmark configuration and minimum GPU estimate by EOD Wed (6/23).
3) Run a 2-hour benchmark window next week (I propose Mon 6/27 10:00-12:00 PT).
4) Post-run: we’ll complete the SLO matrix and map cost/latency tradeoffs.

If any of the baseline SLOs above are off for you, please flag — especially the 150 ms P99 for short streaming paths.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: SLO matrix & streaming constraints for OpsCloud integration

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side after we synced with the platform team: 

- The interactive widget is latency-sensitive: any end-to-end hold over 500 ms for initial token display causes measurable drop in utility. So while 150 ms P99 is ideal, we need to understand what tradeoffs are realistic for different model sizes.
- For background batch generation, 1s P99 is fine.
- Concurrency: our baseline is 50 but note that during marketing events we’ve seen bursts that behave like short-lived spikes to 180–220 concurrent sessions for ~20 minutes.
- Streaming: must be via websocket or SSE with < 250 ms to first token for the interactive path.

We’ll share the prompt CSV and a simple hour-by-hour traffic sketch by EOD Tuesday (6/22). Also, please give us an order-of-magnitude GPU count for the dedicated pool so our procurement and infra teams can scope estimates.

Thanks —
Claire
Claire Jensen
VP Platform, OpsCloud
claire@opscloud.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <claire@opscloud.io>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: SLO matrix & streaming constraints for OpsCloud integration

Claire / Sofia —

Thanks — wanted to add technical color so expectations match reality and to propose a concrete canary plan. Short answers first, then details:

Short answers:
- 150 ms P99 for short prompts is achievable for smaller models (e.g., 7B-13B families) on optimized runtimes with streaming, batching tuned, and sufficient GPUs. For larger families (70B+) expect P99 closer to 300–700 ms depending on quantization and sequence length.
- First-token latency is dominated by tokenizer + initial forward pass; streaming helps because we can emit tokens as soon as partial decoding finishes (reduces perceived latency dramatically).
- For your mix (70% short, 30% up to 8k), a dedicated pool of 4x A10s (or 2x A100s) is a reasonable starting point for throughput ~1k req/min with 50 concurrency and modest batching. To handle 2.5k req/min bursts and spikes to 200 concurrency, plan for 8x A10s (or equivalent) with autoscale policies.

Why latency grows with context:
- Attention compute scales roughly O(N^2) in sequence length; 8k contexts add nontrivial token compute especially in the decode loop. The practical impact is higher P99 and memory pressure which affects batching efficiency.

Tradeoffs & mitigation:
- Quantization (int8) reduces GPU memory & allows bigger batching with modest latency impact; for some workloads int8 can increase initial latency slightly but improves throughput.
- Prefix / KV caching for session-based users will cut repeated prompt cost by 30–60% (depends on how much is static). We recommend caching the retrieval chunk outputs upstream of the model where possible.
- Streaming + early token emission: configure the client to accept partial chunks; server-side we can tune buffer sizes to optimize first-token vs throughput.

Proposed canary benchmark (what Redwood will run):
1) Use your sample prompts (please include distribution).
2) Run three model configs: 13B int8, 33B int8, 70B fp16/quantized (if allowed).
3) Measure P50/P95/P99 first-token and end-to-end for three sequence buckets: <512, 512–2048, 2048–8192.
4) Simulate traffic shapes: steady 1k req/min, 2.5k burst for 15 minutes, spike to 200 concurrency for 20 minutes.
5) Deliver a filled SLO matrix and recommended dedicated pool sizing with cost approximation.

I’ve attached a short perf profile (redwood_perf_profiles_q3.pdf) with recent numbers we can use as priors. I’ll prepare a more detailed runbook and a suggested GPU config table and share by EOD Wed (6/23).

Ticket: SUP-7893 (benchmark + canary).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
